headline_marked: Australia's [[Cummins, Hazlewood, Lyon return]] for Bangladesh Test series after injury layoffs
headline: Australia's Cummins, Hazlewood, Lyon return for Bangladesh Test series after injury layoffs
summary: Captain Pat Cummins, Josh Hazlewood, and Nathan Lyon are back in the Test squad for the two-match series against Bangladesh next month, following significant injury absences.
details: Australia's veteran bowling trio – captain Pat Cummins, Josh Hazlewood, and Nathan Lyon – have been named in the Test squad to face Bangladesh next month. All three return from injury, bolstering the team for the two-match series starting August 13 in Darwin and Mackay. Ashes pace hero Michael Neser was left out, with Scott Boland joining as the fourth seamer.

The trio has faced significant injury setbacks over the past year. Hazlewood, 35, missed the Ashes and T20 World Cup, with his last Test appearance in July 2025. Cummins, 33, has been out since December 2025 due to a back stress complaint, while Lyon, 38, suffered a hamstring tear requiring surgery in the same match.

Chair of selectors George Bailey stated that the players "worked extremely hard, individually and with the SSSM teams over the past few months to return from their respective injuries." He also noted that while it's a 13-player squad, other players are prepared for any necessary adjustments.

Cricket Australia plans to manage the "ageing trio" carefully, anticipating a busy 12-month period that could include up to 21 Tests if they reach next year's World Test Championship final. This cautious approach aims to ensure their longevity and availability for crucial matches.

Meanwhile, opening batsman Usman Khawaja retired after the Ashes triumph in January, leaving a top-order spot open alongside Travis Head. Jake Weatherald is a potential opener, with all-rounder Cameron Green or Marnus Labuschagne possibly batting at number three.

headline_marked: Titumir College students [[protest against high hall fees]]
headline: Titumir College students protest against high hall fees
summary: Students are demanding a significant fee reduction after a recent administration update cut costs by only 200 taka.
details: Students of Titumir College in Dhaka gathered in front of the hall gate on Monday night to protest high hall fees.
The students claim that while other colleges under the Dhaka Central University charge 6,000 taka, Titumir College charges 8,000 taka.
Protesters stated that they are struggling to afford the current costs and are demanding a fair reduction in fees.
Following several days of protests, the college administration promised a fee reduction, but a new notification revealed a cut of only 200 taka.
Students described the administration's action as a 'farce' and have now called for the resignation of the college principal.
caption:
From 8,000 to 7,800 taka? Titumir College students are outraged over a 'farce' of a fee reduction.

Students of Titumir College in Dhaka gathered in front of the hall gate on Monday night to protest high hall fees.

The students claim that while other colleges under the Dhaka Central University charge 6,000 taka, Titumir College charges 8,000 taka.

Protesters stated that they are struggling to afford the current costs and are demanding a fair reduction in fees.

Following several days of protests, the college administration promised a fee reduction, but a new notification revealed a cut of only 200 taka.

Students described the administration's action as a 'farce' and have now called for the resignation of the college principal.
